slides.teach: Build a side-by-side distinction: purpose, strengths, weaknesses, and the scenario where each option fits best.
defs: Using a hypervisor to run multiple virtual machines, usually with separate guest operating systems, on shared hardware.

slides.teach: Build a side-by-side distinction: purpose, strengths, weaknesses, and the scenario where each option fits best.

course.learn: Virtual machines emulate hardware and run separate guest operating systems. Containers share the host kernel while isolating processes and filesystems, making them lighter but more dependent on host security.
course.why: The isolation boundary determines what happens if a workload escapes or the host is compromised.
course.example: Ten containers share one Linux kernel, while ten VMs each have their own guest OS above the hypervisor.
course.exam: VM escape targets VM/hypervisor isolation; container escape reaches the shared host. Images, registries, secrets, and runtime permissions matter for containers.
